speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what are the top five agencies commonly referred to by the Municipal Services Office (MSO) in relation to cases lodged through the OneService app for the past three years; (b) what is the average time taken to close the feedback loop for those cases from each of those five agencies; and (c) whether the MSO independently tracks, audits or verifies that the feedback has been acted upon by the relevant agency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (the Minister for the National Development)
text: Such cases usually involve only one agency and are of a nature where clear, concrete actions can be taken to resolve the issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (the Minister for the National Development)
text: For example, repairing faulty lighting or a broken footpath.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (the Minister for the National Development)
text: This focus on true case resolution has been well-received by residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (the Minister for the National Development)
text: For such cases, time is needed for thorough investigation and enforcement action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (the Minister for the National Development)
text: In such instances, MSO tracks the recurrence of the issue and works with the relevant agencies to better tackle the root causes.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that efficient and effective resolution of the issues much depend on the accurate characterisation and the details to be given.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, I can imagine it will be challenging for officers and agencies to route to the correct channels if such details are not given.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My questions are for the OneService app, how can it be further improved and would there be plans to further improve the app to ensure that users provide all the necessary information upfront and the details – perhaps by the use of ChatBots or AI or any other technology.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And lastly, we should leverage on community resources.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the local grassroots advisors be alerted where key issues on the ground crop up through the OneService app, so that we can leverage on our local resource partners and other community resources on the ground?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For instance, in Keat Hong constituency, we have an estates task force made up of resident volunteers and some community leaders that actually complement the work of the grassroots advisors.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Zhulkarnain, if I could ask you to wrap up, please.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Of the use of AI, that has already being done, for instance, through our OneService Kaki ChatBot.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The ChatBot does use AI to prompt the feedback provider to give more details that allow us or our agencies to identify the location of the case being reported better.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, that is an example of how we are using AI.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of interim updates: first, agencies can use the interim update function that is within the app, to provide some update to our feedback providers before the case is completely resolved.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Also, for the high volume type of cases, when the case is being submitted, that will be a link appearing to a Ministry of National Development (MND) website, where, if the feedback providers so wishes, he can be informed on which are the types of cases that might take longer to resolve and why.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Zhulkarnain also mentioned about the use of community resources and keeping grassroots advisors in the loop.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I am very encouraged to hear that he has a community task force and my team would be glad to discuss how we can support each other in better resolving municipal feedback cases.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of the volume that we handle, it is very high on a daily basis.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, I think we would have to think about how to provide the information in a more summarised form, for ease of partners that wish to work with us.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have two supplementary questions in relation to the OneService app.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The first is, what is the current subscription rate for the OneService app?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second one is, apart from reporting a municipal issue, which my Parliamentary colleague has raised earlier, the OneService app provides many other useful services, such as rendering help to your neighbours and also in terms of finding out which are the nearest useful facilities near you.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, I wish to ask are there any plans to increase awareness and the take-up rates and whether more such useful services will be included in the app in due course?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We look forward to more of such collaborative opportunities so that we can leverage on the large user base to help improve lives for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will continue to take in more suggestions and feedback and I thank Members for being so supportive of the OneService app.
